slides.title: An artificial neuron combines weighted inputs, bias, and activation
slides.visibleText:
EACH CONNECTION CONTRIBUTES XᵢWᵢ BEFORE ACTIVATION.
net = Σᵢ wᵢxᵢ + b
Inputs encode measured evidence.
Weights encode influence and direction.
Bias moves the decision point.
Activation converts the score to an output.

slides.title: Change one factor and watch the score cross threshold
Fixed weights and bias implement AND and OR
slides.visibleText:
AND USES BIAS −2; OR USES BIAS −1 WHEN BOTH INPUT WEIGHTS ARE 1.
f(net) = 1 when net ≥ 0; otherwise 0

The activation rule stays fixed. The bias changes which truth-table rows reach net ≥ 0.

slides.title: One perceptron represents only a linear boundary
slides.visibleText:
CAN REPRESENT
Linearly separable
AND, OR, and the ten-point binary example.
CANNOT REPRESENT
XOR with one unit
Positive corners are opposite; no single line separates them.

slides.title: The XOR threshold inequalities contradict one another
slides.visibleText:
XOR ASSIGNS THE SAME CLASS TO OPPOSITE CORNERS.
w₁+w₂ < θ
w₁ > θ
w₂ > θ
0 < θ

The requirements contradict one another.

actions.stateText: Step Sigmoid ReLU ACTIVATION Step f(z)=1 if z≥0, else 0 Discrete and useful for threshold logic, but it has no usable derivative at the jump.

actions.label: Show sigmoid
actions.stateText: Step Sigmoid ReLU ACTIVATION Sigmoid σ(z)=1/(1+e⁻ᶻ) Smooth, differentiable, and bounded between 0 and 1.

actions.label: Show ReLU
actions.stateText: Step Sigmoid ReLU ACTIVATION ReLU ReLU(z)=max(0,z) A modern hidden-layer choice with a simple positive-side derivative.
